directory_relationships.notes: Opt-in GET-only security-group members/owners and application-registration owners. At most 100 groups and 100 applications are expanded, with --top limiting each inventory and relationship; unbounded --top still caps each relationship at 5000. Limit hits and unreadable links remain explicit coverage gaps. No role assignment, license assignment, credentials or message/file content.

identity.notes: Read-only endpoint set; requires at least directory read permissions in app registration. AuditLog.Read.All plus Microsoft Entra ID P1/P2 adds user signInActivity for stale-account findings; without it identity still runs and records a coverage gap.

security.notes: Sign-in and directory audit data is typically available for read-only security roles with audit permissions.

conditional_access.notes: Conditional Access policy graph endpoints are policy-scoped and may require policy admin or equivalent directory read roles. GET /policies/identitySecurityDefaultsEnforcementPolicy (security defaults) needs only Policy.Read.All.

defender.notes: Defender alerts (alerts_v2), incidents and secure score APIs are covered by Security Reader in most environments. The legacy /security/alerts API retires on 2026-10-15.

service_health.notes: Service health and message center data is available in read-only audit scenarios when reporting permissions are granted.

purview.notes: Most collector commands are CLI-driven and require authenticated M365 CLI session plus app-level Purview/eDiscovery permissions.
optional_commands: m365 purview dlp policy list --output json

ediscovery.notes: Export and hold operations may be CLI-driven and require additional compliance/eDiscovery tenant permissions.
optional_commands: m365 purview ediscovery case list --output json
m365 purview ediscovery search list --output json
m365 purview ediscovery reviewset list --output json

auth_methods.notes: Authentication method policy and registration reports can require report-reading access. The registration report is read with a fixed $select of metadata fields (userType and isAdmin included) and returns no authentication method values. Policy.Read.All also reads whole typed authentication method configurations from /policies/authenticationMethodsPolicy/authenticationMethodConfigurations (v1.0); no per-user method values are read.

reports_usage.notes: Global Reader can access tenant-level usage reporting, while detailed report visibility often requires Reports Reader or a workload-specific reader role. ReportSettings.Read.All reads /admin/reportSettings first; when displayConcealedNames is true, per-user report rows are hashed and Auditex records reports_usage.concealed_names.

external_identity.notes: External identity policy inventory covers cross-tenant access, invitation policy, and authentication flow posture.

consent_policy.notes: Consent policy inventory covers admin consent workflow and permission grant policies. Directory.Read.All reads beta /settings, retaining only EnableAdminConsentRequests values. Policy.Read.All reads default and custom application management policies and ids-only appliesTo targets (at most 100 policies and 50 targets per policy); failures and bounds are coverage gaps.

cross_tenant_access.notes: Cross-tenant access settings are read via /policies/crossTenantAccessPolicy and surface default and partner-scoped trust posture.

domains_hybrid.notes: Hybrid posture is inferred from domains and sampled on-premises sync markers on users.

dns_posture.notes: Resolves email-auth DNS records (SPF, DKIM, DMARC, MTA-STS, TLS-RPT, BIMI) over DoH for verified tenant domains. Live runs also make unauthenticated, read-only HTTPS GETs for those verified domains only: the MTA-STS policy file (https://mta-sts.<domain>/.well-known/mta-sts.txt, only when the _mta-sts TXT record exists, no redirects) and the public Entra OpenID discovery document (https://login.microsoftonline.com/<domain>/v2.0/.well-known/openid-configuration). No usernames are probed. Offline runs make no lookups. Complete TXT answers from public DNS (no sign-in) are saved for SPF, DKIM and DMARC for the verified domains whose Graph supportedServices list includes Email (a domain without that field is kept); posture checks still cover every verified domain.

intune.notes: Will return empty/unavailable datasets if tenant lacks Intune licensing. No scope beyond the three above is needed for the device posture fields (managedDevices $select: isEncrypted, jailBroken, managedDeviceOwnerType, enrolledDateTime, deviceEnrollmentType, lastSyncDateTime), the compliance policy assignments (GET /deviceManagement/deviceCompliancePolicies/{id}/assignments, DeviceManagementConfiguration.Read.All) or the Defender antivirus state (GET /deviceManagement/managedDevices/{id}/windowsProtectionState for at most 100 Windows devices, DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All). The Intune reports API (reports/getDefenderAgentsReport, reports/exportJobs) is a POST export job and is not used.

sharepoint.notes: SharePoint tenant settings and site inventory can vary by role and service readiness.

sharepoint_access.notes: Sampled site permissions are attempted in a reader-first mode, but Graph site permission depth can require stronger SharePoint privileges or app-only escalation.

onedrive_posture.notes: OneDrive posture uses SharePoint read APIs and site URL heuristics; admin-center-only OneDrive details may still be unavailable to Global Reader.

power_bi.notes: Opt-in extended scope, off by default; commercial cloud only. App mode obtains its own token via app_token_for for https://analysis.windows.net/powerbi/api/.default. Customer one-time setup: create a plain Entra security group (no role assignment), add the service principal, then in Power BI Admin portal > Tenant settings > Admin API settings enable "Service principals can access read-only admin APIs" for that specific security group. No Power BI API permission is required; never grant Tenant.Read.All. The alternative operator role is Fabric Administrator with a Power BI or Fabric licence and one prior Power BI portal sign-in, but Auditex has no delegated token path: all eight MS.POWERBI policies stay not assessed on delegated runs. Fabric Administrator is a write-capable admin role used read-only; its blast radius includes tenant-wide Power BI/Fabric administration. The service-principal setting grants access to tenant-wide read-only admin metadata for the group. Auditex uses only GET /v1/admin/tenantsettings and derives accessState locally; no tenant writes, message bodies or file content. Use --collector-preset power-platform deliberately; without the opt-in, optional Power BI / Power Platform collection was not enabled and these policies are not assessed.

power_platform.notes: Opt-in extended scope, off by default; commercial cloud only. The collector obtains its own token in app mode via app_token_for for https://service.powerapps.com//.default; no manually supplied bearer token or new Graph application permission is required. Customer one-time setup: an authorised Power Platform Administrator signs in with Add-PowerAppsAccount -Endpoint prod -TenantID <tenant id>, then registers the customer-owned audit app using New-PowerAppManagementApp -ApplicationId <app id>. This is a customer-side write, never run by Auditex. The management app registration includes write privileges; its blast radius is UNKNOWN beyond that statement. The alternative operator role is Power Platform Administrator with a Power Apps for Office 365 licence; it permits tenant-wide environment and policy administration and is a write-capable admin role used read-only. Auditex has no delegated token path: all seven supported MS.POWERPLATFORM policies stay not assessed on delegated runs. Auditex itself writes nothing. Its BAP sessions use GET only: environments and listTenantSettings (2023-06-01), DLP summaries (2020-10-01), apiPolicies (2016-11-01), tenantIsolationPolicy (2020-06-01). listTenantSettings is a read; TENANT_SETTINGS_METHOD remains pinned GET. POST is only a possible later fallback if GET is refused, to be decided after a playground check; no automatic POST fallback. The companion Power BI audience is https://analysis.windows.net/powerbi/api/.default. No message bodies or file content. Use --collector-preset power-platform deliberately; without the opt-in, optional Power BI / Power Platform collection was not enabled and these policies are not assessed.

sentinel_xdr.notes: Capability-gated. Reads /security/incidents and /security/alerts_v2 from Microsoft Graph; tenants without unified XDR / Sentinel ingestion will yield empty results, surfaced as 'service_not_available' diagnostics.

identity_protection.notes: Capability-gated. Reads one page of GET /identityProtection/riskyUsers (Graph v1.0, read-only) and keeps aggregate counts only; no user names or UPNs are stored. Requires Microsoft Entra ID P2; a licensing error is reported as risk detection 'off', permission errors as 'unknown'.

defender_cloud_apps.notes: Capability-gated. Reads pending app consent requests only. Microsoft Graph has no documented REST endpoint for Defender for Cloud Apps app risk profiles, so those are not collected; review them in the Defender portal.

copilot_governance.notes: Capability-gated. Reads /copilot/admin/settings/limitedMode (delegated only; app-only runs record a coverage gap) and the aggregate /copilot/reports/getMicrosoft365CopilotUserCountSummary CSV. No per-user Copilot activity or interaction content is read. Requires Microsoft 365 Copilot licensing; failure modes map to 'service_not_available'.

teams.notes: Teams endpoints are still readable in many read-only role patterns.

teams_policy.notes: App-only policy reads use a certificate-authenticated Teams admin API token for resource 48ac35b8-9aa8-4d74-927d-1f4a14a0b239 and Global Reader on the service principal, in commercial and GCC only. No Graph scope is required. Without that token and role, rows are coverage gaps (teams_token_unavailable, session_not_connected or command_not_authenticated). The current CLI only acquires client-secret resource tokens, so this read stays unavailable until a certificate-capable client supplies the token; client-secret acceptance is not verified live and is disabled. Messaging and app setup keep their existing command path. Org-wide tenant_app_settings are not collected on app-only runs.

app_consent.notes: Enterprise application consent depth depends on delegated grant and app role assignment visibility. Application.Read.All resolves the eight risky resource app IDs and reads all their delegated permission classifications (v1.0), without filtering by classification or risk; missing resource principals are legal, failed reads are coverage gaps.

app_credentials.notes: Application credential hygiene reads passwordCredentials, keyCredentials, redirect URIs, federatedIdentityCredentials, and owner counts via Microsoft Graph. AuditLog.Read.All enables the Graph beta servicePrincipalSignInActivities report used for dormant-application findings; when unavailable the collector records a coverage gap and the dormant rule stays inert.

licensing.notes: License assignment details are sampled and can be cross-correlated with SKU inventory.

identity_governance.notes: Governance and PIM schedule visibility depends on Entra ID Governance licensing and role-scoped APIs. The PIM role policy reads of the directory roles are covered by RoleManagement.Read.Directory, so an existing registration needs no change; RoleManagementPolicy.Read.Directory is the least-privilege alternative for those policy reads on a new registration (the schedule reads still need RoleManagement.Read.Directory). PIM for Groups policies (RoleManagementPolicy.Read.AzureADGroup) are not read.

intune_depth.notes: Deeper Intune policy and assignment surfaces can still return empty or partial results when Intune is not licensed or the tenant does not use those workloads. groupPolicyConfigurations, deviceManagementScripts, windowsQualityUpdateProfiles and windowsFeatureUpdateProfiles are Graph beta endpoints; script metadata is read with a fixed $select that excludes scriptContent. Windows Update for Business update rings are read from the deviceConfigurations list already collected (type windowsUpdateForBusinessConfiguration, v1.0), and the assignments of each ring and update profile are read with GET .../assignments (DeviceManagementConfiguration.Read.All); no new scope is needed.

exchange.notes: Command-based Exchange posture relies on Microsoft 365 CLI tenant and report commands; mailbox presence falls back to Graph only when CLI reporting is unavailable.
optional_commands: m365 outlook report mailboxusagemailboxcount --period D30 --output json
m365 outlook report mailboxusagedetail --period D30 --output json
m365 outlook report mailboxusagequotastatusmailboxcounts --period D30 --output json
m365 outlook report mailboxusagestorage --period D30 --output json
m365 outlook report mailactivitycounts --period D30 --output json

mailbox_forwarding.notes: Inbox rules (messageRules) and mailbox settings are read with the MailboxSettings.Read permission (application or delegated). Mail.Read is never requested: the audit does not read message content.

exchange_policy.notes: Exchange policy depth uses read-only Exchange PowerShell Get-* cmdlets and requires PowerShell plus Exchange connectivity. Detection-coverage cmdlets (Get-AdminAuditLogConfig, Get-OrganizationConfig, Get-MailboxAuditBypassAssociation counted only) need an Exchange Online PowerShell session; Get-ProtectionAlert is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell (Connect-IPPSSession). Mail protection cmdlets Get-MalwareFilterPolicy, Get-TransportConfig, Get-CASMailbox (a count of the mailboxes that switch SMTP AUTH back on, never an address) and Get-DkimSigningConfig run in the same Exchange Online session and are readable with the Global Reader role the other Exchange cmdlets already use; they need no Graph scope and no further role. None of these cmdlets change tenant state; a missing session is reported as an 'unknown' detection signal and 'not_assessed' mail protection rules, never 'off' or a pass. Partner-sharing domain names and actions are read via Get-SharingPolicy (Name, Domains), readable with Global Reader, the role ScubaGear's own prerequisites list for this cmdlet; no message content is read. Defender for Office 365 / EOP policy reads use the same Exchange Online session (Exchange.ManageAsApp plus Global Reader), add no Graph scope and are read-only. A licence limit is inferred only when both ATP licence-check reads fail with command_error after a healthy eopProtectionPolicyRules read; reclassified envelopes retain the error text and carry licence_inferred: true. Authentication, session and command_not_found failures remain coverage gaps; the real unlicensed-tenant error class is unverified. IPPS is OFF by default: AUDITEX_ENABLE_IPPS=true explicitly enables the three Security & Compliance reads (Get-ProtectionAlert, Get-DlpCompliancePolicy, Get-DlpComplianceRule). Certificate only: AZURE_CLIENT_ID, AUDITEX_IPPS_ORGANIZATION (initial onmicrosoft domain), exactly one of AUDITEX_IPPS_CERTIFICATE_THUMBPRINT (Windows certificate store only) or AUDITEX_IPPS_CERTIFICATE_FILE (PFX, macOS/Linux) plus AUDITEX_IPPS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD_ENV (name of its password variable). PFX must be a non-empty regular file, owned by the current user with no group/other permissions, at most 64 KiB; symlinks are refused. Password is consumed into memory at live audit/probe entry before auth, toolchain or collector children and supplied only to IPPS children, never argv/logs. Connect-IPPSSession uses -CertificateFilePath and -CertificatePassword with an environment-derived SecureString; provider key-store behaviour is unverified. Portable module/certificate support is inferred from documentation, not live-tested; prove it in the macOS playground. Missing/conflicting selectors fail as missing_app_credentials. Exchange.ManageAsApp and Entra Global Reader are the pinned ScubaGear noninteractive requirements, not proof of minimal IPPS RBAC. Purview View-Only Configuration, View-Only DLP and View-Only Manage Alerts are candidate narrower role assignments (Inference, app-only support unverified); Compliance Administrator is broader and not established as minimum. Confirm exact cmdlet grants with the customer before enabling; no automatic role changes. Locations keep All and same-length scope placeholders; NotifyUser keeps cardinality only. Nested lists explicitly preserve zero/one/many entries. DLP policy projection requires AuditexExceptionPropertiesAvailable=true from original PowerShell property metadata; absent/unknown availability and populated exceptions withhold it. AdvancedRule is omitted and advanced rules are not assessed. No new Graph permission.
